-10.help: Encode with decimal instead of hex

-32.help: Encode with base32 instead of hex

-64.help: Encode with base64 instead of hex

-8.help: Encode with octal instead of hex

-C.help: Recursively CHECK directory against list of files on stdin

-Cf.help: Recursively CHECK directory against list but only show failures

-S.help: Strict mode: when checking, check file mtime, owner, group, and inode as well as its hash

-X.help: Exclude items matching shell patters stored in <file>

-attrs.help: comma-separated list of filesystem attribute names to be set to the value of the hash.

-base32.help: Encode with base32 instead of hex

-base64.help: Encode with base64 instead of hex

-c.help: CHECK hashes against list from file (or stdin)

-c32.help: Encode with Crockford base32 instead of hex

-cache.help: Use hashes stored in 'user' xattr if they're younger than the mtime of the file. This speeds up outputting hashes. Also do not update xattr of a file if it already matches.

-cf.help: CHECK hashes against list but only show failures

-clip.help: Update X11 clipboard to the current hash. This works using the 'xsel', 'xclip' or 'pbcopy' commands, or if none of those are installed falls back to Xterm clipboard as in the '-xsel' option .

-color.help: Use ANSI color codes on output when checking hashes.

-devmode.help: DevMode: read from a file EVEN IF IT'S A DEVNODE

-dir.help: DirMode: Read all files in directory and create one hash for them!

-dirmode.help: DirMode: Read all files in directory and create one hash for them!

-exec.help: In CHECK or MATCH mode only examine executable files.

-h.help: Script to run when a file fails CHECK mode, or is found in MATCH mode.

-hide-input.help: When reading data from stdin in linemode, set the terminal to not echo characters, thus hiding typed input.

-hook.help: Script to run when a file fails CHECK mode, or is found in FIND mode

-i.help: Only hash items matching a comma-seperated list of shell patterns

-i64.help: Encode with base64 with rearranged characters

-idfile.help: Path to an ssh private key file to use to authenticate INSTEAD OF A PASSWORD when pulling files via ssh.

-lines.help: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly.

-list-hashes.help: Print a list of hashes that can be used with the '-type' option

-lm.help: Read hashes from stdin, upload them to a memcached server (requires the -memcached option).

-m.help: MATCH files from a list read from stdin.

-mcd.help: Specify memcached server. (Overrides reading list from stdin if used with -m, -c or -cf).

-mmin.help: <mins>   Only hash items <min> minutes old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten mins, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten mins old

-mtime.help: Only hash items <days> old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten days, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten days old

-myear.help: Only hash items <years> old. Has the same format as the find command, e.g. -10 is younger than ten years, +10 is older than ten, and 10 is ten years old

-name.help: <patterns> Only hash items matching a comma-seperated list of shell patterns (-name aka 'find')

-net.help: Treat 'file' arguments as either ssh or http URLs, and pull files over the network and then hash them (Allows hashing of files on remote machines). URLs are in the format ssh://[username]:[password]@[host]:[port] or http://[username]:[password]@[host]:[port]..

-p64.help: Encode with base64 with a-z,A-Z and _-, for best compatibility with 'allowed characters' in websites.

-period.help: produce otp codes with period/lifetime of <n> seconds

-qr.help: Display the current hash as a qrcode. This requires the 'qrencode' command to be installed, and also an image viewer like fim, feh, or imagemagick display to be installed.

-qrcode.help: Display the current hash as a qrcode. This requires the 'qrencode' command to be installed, and also an image viewer like fim, feh, or imagemagick display to be installed.

-r.help: Recurse into directories when hashing files

-r64.help: Encode with base64 with a-z,A-Z and _-, rfc4648 compatible.

-rawlines.help: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly, INCLUDING any trailing whitespace. (This is compatible with 'echo text | md5sum')

-rfc4648.help: Encode with base64 with a-z,A-Z and _-, rfc4648 compatible.

-rl.help: Read lines from stdin and hash each line independantly, INCLUDING any trailing whitespace. (This is compatible with 'echo text | md5sum')

-star-input.help: When reading data from stdin in linemode replace characters with stars.

-strict.help: Strict mode: when checking, check file mtime, owner, group, and inode as well as its hash

-t.help: Output hashes in traditional md5sum, shaXsum format

-totp.help: TOTP code with secret, defaults to google-authenticator compatible setup

-trad.help: Output hashes in traditional md5sum, shaXsum format

-txattr.help: Use TRUSTED eXtended file ATTRibutes. In hash mode, store hashes in 'trusted' file attributes. 'trusted' attributes can only be read and written by root. Under freebsd this menas SYSTEM attributes.

-type.help: specify a hash type to use. This supports hashes coming from other subsystems, such as openssl. It also supports 'chaining' hash types like so: -type sha256,whirl

-u.help: Update. In checking mode, update hashes for the files as you go. <types> is a comma-separated list of things to update, which can be 'xattr' 'memcached' or a file name. This will update these targets with the hash that was found at the time of checking.

-w32.help: Encode with word-safe base32 instead of hex

-x.help: Exclude items matching a comma-sepearted list of shell patterns

-xattr.help: Use eXtended file ATTRibutes. In hash mode, store hashes in the file attributes, in check mode compare against hashes stored in file attributes.

-xdialog.help: Run in 'xdialog' (zenity, yad or qarama) mode

-xsel.help: Update X11 clipboard and primary selections to the current hash. This works using Xterm command sequences. The xterm resource 'allowWindowOps' must be set to 'true' for this to work.

-z32.help: Encode with zbase32 instead of hex

-z85.help: Encode with ZEROMQ variant of ASCII85.
